$comment: Licence decisions somebody made by reading a publisher's terms. The register's own build generates every decision as `unchecked` from the research pass's access labels, which is correct — that pass recorded what a register costs to reach and opened nobody's terms. This file is where a decision that was made gets recorded, and `buildSourceRegister` applies these over the generated defaults. It is an input to the build rather than an edit of its output, so a rebuild preserves what is here instead of overwriting it.
$howToAdd: Read the publisher's terms. Store the copy you read somewhere a later reader can open it, and name that location in `retrievedCopy` — a link to today's page is not a copy. Then add one entry here keyed by the `licenseID` the register already uses for that source, and rebuild. `auditAddressSourceRegister` refuses an elected record missing `electedTerms`, `retrievedCopy` or `electedBecause`, and a refused record missing `refusedBecause`, so an incomplete entry fails the build rather than entering the register.
$shape: Each key is a licenseID the register declares. Each value is an ElectedLicense or RefusedLicense minus its `licenseID`, which the build fills from the key. See `@mailwoman/corpus/source-register`'s types.
$titleIsNotThePublisher: Find a publisher's own licence entry by matching the publisher rather than the product's title. Two data.gov.uk entries describe the Companies House Free Company Data Product. The one whose title matches the product name is published by the London Borough of Barnet and reads `license_id: notspecified`. The one that licenses it is published by Companies House, is titled `Basic Company Data`, and reads `license_id: cc-by`. Reading the title-matching entry would have recorded that no licence exists.
$state: Thirty-four decisions are recorded here and three shared readings under `sharedReadings`, which the build expands to 28 elected and 6 refused licences over the register's 399 sources. Elected are ten INSPIRE Addresses themes, under CC0 1.0 for the Netherlands and Estonia, CC BY 4.0 for Denmark and Navarra, CC BY-SA 4.0 for Gipuzkoa, the INSPIRE controlled value for an absence of conditions for Czechia and Slovakia, the Modellicentie voor gratis hergebruik Vlaanderen v1.0 for the Flemish Region, and each publisher's own access-and-use licence for Catastro and Bizkaia; AusTender under CC BY 3.0 AU; DENUE under INEGI's own free-use terms; SIRENE under Licence Ouverte 2.0 in each of nine overseas territories; five OCDS procurement releases under CC0 1.0 (Chile, Germany), CC BY 4.0 (Italy, Zambia) and the Licencia de Datos Abiertos Uruguay 0.1; Svalbard's Enhetsregisteret records under NLOD 2.0; and Companies House's Free Company Data Product under Creative Commons Attribution. Refused are the Banque Centrale des Comores, the Institut de la statistique de la Polynésie française, the Government of Tokelau, Kenya's PPRA, the Central Bank of Libya and Kosovo's PPRC, each of which reserves rights and publishes no data licence. Electing terms is necessary and not sufficient: `ingestEligibilityProblems` also requires a resolved address role per column, measured coverage, and a personal-data review that is not `present`, which no licence decision touches. Those live in `source-resolutions.json`. `mwops release rights-audit` reports 11 of 399 sources eligible for ingest. See #2351 for this file and #2323 for the source fields.
$notElected:
Three candidates examined across 2026-09-30 remain unchecked, and each is unchecked for a different reason. The Puerto Rico Department of State's corporations registry states nothing either way: its 646,949 bytes carry one licensing string, `Licensed under MIT`, which is Bootstrap's notice inside a stylesheet comment rather than a statement about the registry, and the territory's data catalog answers HTTP 404 at its CKAN API. An absence of any statement is a different fact from a reservation of rights, which is why it stays unchecked rather than joining the refusals. Ghana's PPA publication records a licence as a bare URL, `https://www.ppaghana.org/ocds-license`, and that host failed at the network layer from four paths across three passes, so the licence exists and is unreadable. Spain's `es-mixed-regulatory-2` is INE, and no pass has read an INE document; its row exists because the 2026-09-30 rights review split `Catastro, INE` into one row per publisher, and that split is what let Catastro's INSPIRE licence be elected without granting INE's data. Two candidates left this list by being elected. Companies House's Free Company Data Product download page states only the access cost, and Companies House licenses the same product on data.gov.uk as `Basic Company Data` under Creative Commons Attribution. Catastro's licence is elected against `unchecked-access-free-es-direcci-n-general-del-catastro`, and the three foral cadastres that publish through the same national feed are elected separately. Three left it by being refused once the publisher's own words were read rather than a third party's field: Kenya's PPRA reserves all rights in its footer, the Central Bank of Libya reserves all rights in its footer, and Kosovo's PPRC publishes terms whose clause 12(c) reserves copying, reproduction and derivative works except by its express written agreement. Kenya matters as a method note: earlier passes recorded its host as failing at the network layer, which was the `www` prefix, so its terms had never been read rather than been read and found empty. Check a bare host before recording a publisher as unreachable. The retrieved documents are in `internal/strategy/rights-receipts/gb-mx-es-2026-09-30/`, `ocp-eight-2026-09-30/`, `seven-web-sources-2026-09-30/`, `publisher-terms-2026-09-30/`, `es-catastro-2026-09-30/` and `es-foral-cadastres-2026-09-30/`. Request drafts are in `internal/strategy/rights-outreach/2026-09-30-footer-reservations/` for the three publishers that reserve rights in a footer, and in `2026-09-30-no-stated-license/` for the four whose own sites were re-read, where Kosovo's asks for the written agreement its own clause 12(c)(ii) provides for. Two services left this list on 2026-10-01 and both left it the same way, which is the method note worth keeping: the statement existed and the route to it was misread. Flanders' instrument was named in the dataset record, and its identifier served one JavaScript application for every content type, so the text looked unretrievable. Appending `.ttl` to that identifier's path returns the RDF, and the record's `rdfs:seeAlso` gives the page carrying the nine articles. **A single-page application intercepts a path rather than a file extension.** Slovakia's dataset record was recorded as unreachable after the export URL in its own capabilities document answered HTTP 422 four ways. That body says which field is wrong and where it belongs: `{"loc":["path","collection_record_id"],"msg":"value is not a valid uuid"}` places the id in the path where the capabilities put it in the query, and a second 422 enumerates the permitted `export_format` values, which exclude the `gmd` the capabilities asks for. **A 422 is a validation message naming the fix, where a 404 is an absence**, so read the body before recording a publisher as unreachable. Both `data.gov.sk` and `data.slovensko.sk` do answer every path with the same 524-byte application shell, identical by sha256, and neither was the route: `rpi.gov.sk`, the publisher's own register, holds the record.

The Faroe Islands joined this list on 2026-10-01, and the reason is worth separating from the others: the data is fully readable and the grant is missing. Umhvørvisstovan serves Adressuskrá as an ArcGIS MapServer whose service document stamps `copyrightText` `©Umhvørvisstovan`, and 26,471 address points, 30,451 address units and 2,180 street centerlines were read from it without a key. **A copyright notice asserts authorship and grants nothing**, so it cannot be elected terms. The agency's `skilmalar`, `opin-gogn` and `privatlivspolitikkur` paths each answer HTTP 404 behind the same 82,183-byte page, its WordPress search API answers 0 pages for `skilmálar` and for `opin gögn`, and the two pages it does return for `brúksrættur` are the front page and the land-registration page, where the term carries its property-law sense. The Address Act the register page cites, `logir.fo/Logtingslog/17-fra-06-03-2002-um-adressur`, serves a navigation index of the whole statute book rather than the act's text. A statutory duty to maintain a register is a different thing from a license to reuse it in any case. The route to a decision here is the agency itself, at the `adressur@us.fo` address its own page publishes for address submissions, which no one has written to.

Hong Kong joined this list on 2026-10-01, and it is the first entry held back by what a grant leaves out rather than by an absence of one. DATA.GOV.HK's Terms of Use, `https://data.gov.hk/en/terms-and-conditions`, 39,948 bytes, sha256 `c901a8f56c42a4cb`, state: `You are allowed to browse, download, distribute, reproduce, hyperlink to, and print the Data for both commercial and non-commercial purposes on a free-of-charge basis`, against attribution, an acknowledgement of the Government's intellectual property and an indemnity. That is a generous grant and **it enumerates its rights**. The words `adapt`, `modify`, `derivative`, `alter` and `translate` appear nowhere in the document's 9,289 characters of prose, and neither does any prohibition: `shall not` occurs six times and every occurrence is a liability disclaimer. **Two of this register's four `INGEST_OPERATIONS` need adaptation.** Normalising an address into components is a derived work, and training a model on it is another, so `transform` and `train` rest on a permission the terms neither give nor refuse. An enumerated grant that omits an operation is not the same fact as silence about the whole question, and it is not a reservation of rights either, so this stays unchecked with the gap named. The route to a decision is the Digital Policy Office, which publishes `enquiry@1835500.gov.hk`, and the question to ask is narrow: whether reproduction as granted extends to a derived work. Hong Kong's address data is worth that question. `https://www.als.gov.hk/lookup` returns structured premises addresses in English and Chinese together, carrying `EngStreet`, `BuildingNoFrom`, `EngEstate` and `DcDistrict` beside `ChiStreet` and `ChiDistrict`, and `https://portal.csdi.gov.hk/csdi-webpage/` lists `Address` as one of its framework spatial data themes with OGC WFS, WMS, ArcGIS REST and a dataset API, which is the bulk route a later pass should measure.
$sireneRepetition: Nine of the decisions below are one reading of one document, recorded nine times. INSEE publishes SIRENE for mainland France and its overseas territories, and the register scopes a decision to one publisher in one jurisdiction, so BL, GF, GP, MF, MQ, PM, RE, WF and YT each carry their own. That repetition is deliberate: an election wide enough to cover nine jurisdictions at once is the failure review cannot undo.
$sharedReadings: One publisher can hold a licence over several jurisdictions, and the register scopes a decision to one publisher in one jurisdiction, so reading that publisher's terms once produces several decisions with the same body. A decision reads `sameAs` to name a body declared here, which keeps each licence id's own decision while the prose behind it has one home. The build refuses a `sameAs` naming a reading this file does not declare.
$ocpRegistryStatements: Five of the decisions below rest on the OCP Data Registry's own licence statement rather than on the publisher's page. Each of those register rows records its access as OCDS bulk through that registry and its `sourceURL` as the registry, so the copy this repository would fetch is the registry's and the licence it publishes is the one governing that copy. AusTender is the exception: its publisher's own terms were retrieved, which is the stronger record. Retrieving each of the five publishers' own pages would raise them to the same standard and is not done.

Each download ships a `licence.txt`, and each one states `Your use of OS OpenData is subject to the terms at http://os.uk/opendata/licence` (Code-Point Open words it `Your use of data is subject to terms at www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/opendata/licence`). Both addresses redirected on 2026-10-14 to `https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/`, 10,450 bytes, sha256 `f5b2b9f2af63647cde889fa6c3508f5705925295b74912c68caa28dd37e64aa5`. OS's own `docs.os.uk` terms page, 2,936 bytes, sha256 `83e7e1047ff833d4144e451f596290543b5673915733d3a26b8d48cac5253d7e`, states that the OS OpenData terms `are contained within the Open Government Licence` and that the attribution statement `can be found in the licence file downloaded with the data`. The licence files read are Code-Point Open 2026-08, 346 bytes, sha256 `2273fa3818d2b009ab38c11f3cfc9563e48c0e9e940bf73c1a3685b3188255ad`; OS Open Names 2026-07, 438 bytes, sha256 `1be838dcdba14daa10f6a5015833100858711fcda9e495a9442c9295d357f99f`; OS Open Roads 2026-04, 190 bytes, sha256 `65f3f555aa3e42e93b4db24a29ad277beefd12bc4871076d558c1cc41a6b216d`; and OS Open USRN 2026-10, 442 bytes, sha256 `41e89b74974c31cbb39efec9d78db825107e8fca565611e7098f92c94c6be62e`. The attribution differs by product. Open Roads requires `Contains Ordnance Survey data © Crown copyright and database right 2026`. Open USRN requires `Contains OS data © Crown Copyright and database rights 2026` and, `Where you use data relating to Scotland`, `This product contains data created and maintained by Scottish Local Government.` No licence file or page read restricts the Royal Mail-derived postcode data beyond that acknowledgement, which is a statement about the text read; the OGL's own exemption for `third party rights the Information Provider is not authorised to license` stays in force. ocp-registry-cc0-1.0.electedBecause: The OCP Data Registry publishes this OCDS release under CC0 1.0 and offers no alternative: `License: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication`, with the deed's summary that the person associating the work with it `has dedicated the work to the public domain by waiving all of his or her rights to the work worldwide under copyright law, including all related and neighboring rights, to the extent allowed by law`. The legalcode is retained beside the registry page. CC0 imposes no attribution condition, so this repository owes none; crediting the publisher anyway is courtesy rather than obligation.

fetch.because: CC0 waives every copyright and related right to the extent allowed by law, so copying the published file is unrestricted by the dedication.

extract.because: The deed states `You can copy, modify, distribute and perform the work, even for commercial purposes`, and reading columns out of the file is copying and modifying.

transform.because: The deed permits modification without condition.

train.because: CC0 reserves no act, so fitting a model on the rows is unrestricted by the dedication.

redistribute-data.because: The deed permits distribution and performance, commercially included, with no attribution or share-alike condition.

redistribute-model.because: CC0 waives the rights that would make a derived work's release a licensed act, so the question that stays unreviewed under CC BY does not arise here.

commercial-sublicense.because: A dedication to the public domain leaves no right to sublicense, so a recipient needs no grant from this repository.

ocp-registry-cc-by-4.0.electedBecause: The OCP Data Registry publishes this OCDS release under CC BY 4.0 and offers no alternative: `License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)`, with the deed's summary granting `Share — copy and redistribute the material in any medium or format` and `Adapt — remix, transform, and build upon the material for any purpose, even commercially`, under `Attribution — You must give appropriate credit, provide a link to the license, and indicate if changes were made` and `No additional restrictions`. The legalcode is retained beside the registry page. The attribution owed is therefore a credit, a link to the licence, and a statement that changes were made, which a transformed corpus always requires.

fetch.because: CC BY 4.0 grants the right to reproduce and share the material in any medium or format.

extract.because: The grant to `remix, transform, and build upon the material` covers reading the address fields out of the release.

transform.because: The same clause grants adaptation for any purpose, so a token and tag corpus is permitted with the change indicated.

train.because: §2(a)(1)(A) grants reproduction and §2(a)(1)(B) grants producing Adapted Material for any purpose, commercial use included, and fitting a model performs both.

redistribute-data.because: The Share grant covers redistribution in any medium, conditioned on the attribution and on adding no restriction beyond the licence.

redistribute-model.because: Whether trained weights are Adapted Material under CC BY 4.0 is the question `internal/strategy/counsel-briefing-2026-09-27-part-2.md` records, and the deed does not state it. If they are, the attribution and the statement of changes attach to the release.

commercial-sublicense.because: CC BY 4.0 grants no sublicensing right and instead gives every downstream recipient an offer from the licensor directly. Whether that arrangement satisfies a commercial agreement's needs is a drafting question this text does not answer.

ign-ban-lov2-territories.electedBecause: This is the same publisher, the same database and the same instrument as `unchecked-access-free-fr-institut-national-de-l-information-g-ographiq`, applied to ten jurisdictions that the register carries as their own ISO 3166-1 codes. That decision records the reading of IGN's conditions of use at `https://adresse.data.gouv.fr/cgu` and of the dataset's `license` `lov2` on `https://www.data.gouv.fr/api/1/datasets/base-adresse-nationale/`, and it stays the home of the reading for the whole-country extract it was made about. What this body adds is the evidence that the grant reaches these ten territories, which the metropolitan file alone does not show. **The Base Adresse Nationale publishes one gzipped CSV per INSEE department code beside the national extract, at the same path and under the same dataset record.** `https://adresse.data.gouv.fr/data/ban/adresses/latest/csv/` lists 107 department files, among them the three-digit codes 971, 972, 973, 974, 975, 976, 977, 978, 984, 986, 987, 988 and 989. Ten of those answer HTTP 200 with data and all ten carry the same 23-column header as the national file, read from each file rather than assumed: Guadeloupe 163,423 rows, Martinique 138,460, French Guiana 60,904, Réunion 340,941, Saint Pierre and Miquelon 3,049, Mayotte 52,588, Saint Barthélemy 5,553, Saint Martin 7,363, French Polynesia 7,713 and New Caledonia 51,702, which is 831,696 rows measured on 2026-10-01 with no ragged row in any file. `https://api-adresse.data.gouv.fr/search/` returns these as `type` `street` with `context` `987, Polynésie française` and `988, Nouvelle-Calédonie`, so the publisher treats them as part of the same address base rather than as a separate product. IGN's conditions state the institute's mission over `plus de 25 millions d'adresses sur le territoire français`, and the French territories are part of that territory, which is why no separate grant is needed for them. **French Polynesia needs one distinction kept.** The register separately refuses the Institut de la statistique de la Polynésie française, which reserves its rights over its own publications; that is a different publisher from IGN and says nothing about this file. Electing here does not disturb that refusal.

fetch.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 grants the right to reproduce, copy and publish the Information freely and for any purpose, which is what downloading one department's gzipped CSV performs.

extract.because: The same grant covers extracting and transforming the Information, which is reading `numero`, `nom_voie`, `code_postal` and `nom_commune` out of a row.

transform.because: The licence permits adapting, modifying and combining the Information with other information, which is what normalising a row into this repository's components does.

train.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 names no restriction on the purpose of reuse and attaches no share-alike term, so training a model on the Information falls inside `librement, pour tout usage`. The licence's one obligation is attribution of the source and the date of the last update, which the release artifacts carry.

insee-sirene-lov2.electedBecause: SIRENE offers one licence and no alternative. data.gouv.fr's dataset page records `Producteur Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques (Insee)` and `Licence Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0`, and its API answers `license: lov2` for the same dataset. The licence text names SIRENE as its own worked example for attribution: `Dans le cas d'une réutilisation de la base SIRENE de l'INSEE, mentionner l'URL du « Concédant » : www.insee.fr + la date de dernière mise à jour de l'Information réutilisée.` The attribution owed is therefore the source and the date of the last update, and the mention must not suggest official endorsement. No share-alike term applies: the licence states it was designed to be compatible with any free licence requiring attribution at a minimum, naming OGL, CC-BY and ODC-BY. It settles no personal-data question, which it says in terms: personal data `peut être librement réutilisée` only `à condition de respecter le cadre légal relatif à la protection des données à caractère personnel`.

fetch.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 grants the reuser freedom `de la communiquer, la reproduire, la copier`, which is what copying the published stock file performs.

extract.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 grants freedom `de l'adapter, la modifier, l'extraire et la transformer, notamment pour créer des « Informations dérivées »`. Reading the address columns out of the stock file is the `extraire` in that clause.

transform.because: The same clause grants `la transformer, notamment pour créer des « Informations dérivées »`, and the licence defines an `Information dérivée` as any new data created directly from the Information. A token and tag corpus is such a work.

train.because: Fitting a model creates new information directly from the Information, which the licence's own definition of `Information dérivée` covers, and the grant for creating one is unconditional beyond attribution.

redistribute-data.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 grants freedom `de la diffuser, la redistribuer, la publier et la transmettre, de l'exploiter à titre commercial, par exemple en la combinant avec d'autres informations, ou en l'incluant dans votre propre produit ou application`. Commercial reuse and inclusion in a product are named acts, subject to the attribution above.

redistribute-model.because: The licence grants creating an `Information dérivée` and grants redistributing `l'Information`, including by combining it with other information. Whether redistributing trained weights is one of those acts is the question `internal/strategy/counsel-briefing-2026-09-27-part-2.md` records, and this text does not state it. The grant here is wider than CC BY 3.0 AU's, so the answer may differ.

commercial-sublicense.because: The licence grants the reuser a non-exclusive right and states no term about granting that right onward. A recipient of redistributed Information is itself a `Réutilisateur` under the same licence, which is closer to needing no sublicence than to a sublicence being granted, and the text settles neither.

$firstRefusals: Three decisions below read `refused`, the register's first. Each publisher reserves all rights in its own footer and publishes no data license: the Banque Centrale des Comores, the Institut de la statistique de la Polynésie française, and the Government of Tokelau. A footer notice is a site-wide assertion rather than a statement about the data, so a request to the publisher could still produce a grant. What `refused` records is that the terms were read and no grant was found, which is a different state from `unchecked`, where nobody looked.

The SMT conditions, `https://smt.esante.gouv.fr/cgu/` (95,036 bytes, sha256 `dbcb5c85c4e95b697e90721a09bc2d3cdd8c152c30e64af034b3e67bbd26ed2f`), govern the terminology server rather than the mos.esante.gouv.fr files, grant at §10 a `droit d'utilisation du SMT ... pour usage propre` ("right to use the SMT ... for one's own use"), defer to each terminology's own licence, and list `Les dispositions du code des relations entre le public et l'administration (CRPA)` in their applicable legal frame; the SMT catalogue renders its per-terminology licences in script and the retained copy shows none for TRE_R35. ANS is a groupement d'intérêt public, a legal person of public law, so it is an administration under CRPA L. 300-2. The CRPA text retrieved from codes.droit.org (2,931,595 bytes, sha256 `88bd56805aff26399099f6acce38b055d2e2c63242c6bdfbbc85f115145159bb`) reads at L. 321-1 `Les informations publiques figurant dans des documents communiqués ou publiés par les administrations mentionnées au premier alinéa de l'article L. 300-2 peuvent être utilisées par toute personne qui le souhaite à d'autres fins que celles de la mission de service public pour les besoins de laquelle les documents ont été produits ou reçus` ("Public information in documents communicated or published by the administrations named in L. 300-2 may be used by any person who wishes, for purposes other than the public-service mission for which the documents were produced or received"), and at L. 322-1 `Sauf accord de l'administration, la réutilisation des informations publiques est soumise à la condition que ces dernières ne soient pas altérées, que leur sens ne soit pas dénaturé et que leurs sources et la date de leur dernière mise à jour soient mentionnées` ("Unless the administration agrees, reuse is subject to the information not being altered, its meaning not being distorted, and its source and the date of its last update being stated"). L. 321-2 c) excludes information on which third parties hold intellectual property rights; a list of French street-type words authored by ANS carries none that the retrieved documents name. Legifrance answered HTTP 403 to every article URL, so the consolidated text is the codes.droit.org copy.
